scope: Accepted-load power review. Model findings and improvement targets; no circuit changes or hardware qualification.

resolvedTimeouts: PWR_OK, its independent 5 V LED branch, and local ground returns have top-layer copper
all eight PCIe TX capacitor outputs reach the correct slot pads on top without vias

nativePlacementAssessment.finding: Airwire-based orientation heuristic suggests a 180-degree rotation.
nativePlacementAssessment.assessment: Nonpolar capacitor has fixed routed contacts to the correct pads. Geometry, native continuity and DRC audits pass. A rotation requires rerouting and is not an electrical correction to the existing fixed copper.

findings.result: The conservative conductor screen exceeds the 8 mV project limit at 3 A.
findings.target: Review shared feed copper, output contacts and parallel vias. Keep separate transient and ground-return checks.

findings.result: The assumed 1.5 A increase and release exceed the 1.10-1.16 V window in the passive model. A small voltage trim does not fix both extremes.
findings.target: Review effective capacitance, bypass access and converter response. Obtain a usable controller model or bench waveforms before selecting a final remedy.

findings.result: Missing VDD, VDD brownout and a short power cycle expose the RC reset limitations. All 18 normal-startup sensitivity cases pass.
findings.target: A dedicated rail supervisor needs accurate thresholds, suitable timing and enough sink current for the 1 uF reset capacitor. TPS62903 PG thresholds do not enforce the full PDX voltage window.

findings.result: All 96 startup comparison cases settle. Peak current is not a switch-SOA qualification.
findings.target: Compare VDS/current trajectories with temperature-adjusted SOA. Consider controlled inrush if margin is insufficient.

findings.result: The 3 A VDD budget uses the full nominal regulator rating. The bridge rail allowance totals 5.62 W if all loads are sustained.
findings.target: Verify converter derating and the bridge thermal path. Reference-condition arithmetic does not predict assembled-board temperature.

thermalAllowance.limitation: All rail input is treated as local heat. ASMedia reference heatsink values do not predict Flamingo temperatures.

limitations: Selected currents are provisional PDX design assumptions, not measured or guaranteed limits. Idle current, current spectrum and load edge rates are unknown.
TI PSpice SLVMDN8 and SIMPLIS SLVMDP3 packages contain encrypted models. No vendor closed-loop transient simulation was run.
Switching ripple is a forced-PWM triangular-current harmonic calculation. It excludes controller jitter, switch-node coupling, common ground, package and probe noise.

Samsung curves are typical at their stated measurement conditions. Multiplying DC-bias, 10 mV AC, tolerance and temperature factors is a sensitivity construction, not a guaranteed joint capacitor model. Low AC amplitude below 10 mV is outside the published curve.
Switching frequency 2.25–2.75 MHz and inductor 0.72–1.2 uH are sensitivity assumptions. They are not guaranteed switching-frequency limits.

Interconnect inductance 1–20 nH and mounting inductance 0.2–1 nH per capacitor are assumed, not extracted. The 80 C board resistance and mesh allowance come from the previous DC analysis; ground and package losses remain excluded.

The transient network reduces each physical capacitor bank to one series RLC using low-frequency moments and typical ESR at 2.5 MHz. ESR x0.5/x2 and edge-rate cases are separate sensitivities. Distributed branch antiresonance and unequal ball currents remain unmodeled.

Transient source current starts after a prescribed 0–2 us delay, then catches up at the ideal maximum buck slew with a 1.2 uH inductor. This is optimistic after the assumed delay, not a TPS62903 transfer function. It predicts a conditional first dip/peak only; the apparent later offset is not a voltage recovery prediction.
Minimum and maximum voltage corners are evaluated separately. Ripple phase is conservatively aligned with the transient extremum. No pass fraction is a probability.
No startup, short circuit, thermal qualification, complete SI/BER simulation or hardware measurement is added by this analysis.
VCCH/VCCA33 split is unknown; endpoints and midpoint are planning scenarios. Equal current across VCCH balls is assumed.
VCCA33 3.0 V floor follows the 3.3 V-domain project screen; the PDX current table does not supply an independent VCCA33 specification.
50 milliohm jumper resistance is the manufacturer family limit, without a separate hot-resistance model.
Ground, connector/cable, semiconductor package, AC noise, capacitor charging and arbitrary programming-header loads are omitted.
Bridge internal currents and external pin loading are not measured.
Typical vendor model, not a guaranteed production or electrothermal model; 85 C is sensitivity only.
Output ramp time is simulated rather than equated to the gate RC constant. A specific GPU/card, PSU and cable remain unmodeled.
The 1000 uF added card capacitance is an explicit assumption. Larger capacitance and other load timing require another run.
Single-pulse SOA, startup repetition, hot restart, slow shutdown and fault survival still require temperature-aware review and hardware measurements.
No local current limiting exists. Passing the settling screen does not qualify MOSFET SOA or arbitrary card compatibility.
